 Sparta Praha vs. AFC Bournemouth - Head-to-head record
 This will be the first competitive meeting between Sparta Praha and AFC Bournemouth, so there is no previous head-to-head record to consider.
 With no history between the clubs, Thursday’s encounter will be a fresh test for both sides. Current form and their respective performances in the Europa League are likely to be more significant indicators than historical results.

 Sparta Praha - Searching for consistency
 Let’s take a closer look at Sparta Praha’s current situation. We will analyse their latest results and how they might set up for this European test. We will also show you the potential Sparta Praha vs. AFC Bournemouth line-ups.
 Recent form
 Sparta Praha have had an uneven run of results ahead of Thursday’s European fixture. Their last six matches in all competitions have produced two wins, three draws and one defeat, although their recent performances have been particularly disappointing.
 After beating Slovácko 5-1, Brian Priske’s side were eliminated from the Czech Cup with a 2-0 home defeat to Baník Ostrava. They then drew 0-0 away to Bohemians 1905, leaving them eight points behind city rivals Slavia Praha at the top of the Czech First League.
 Their Europa League campaign has also been mixed . Sparta began with a 4-1 away victory over Ararat-Armenia and a 1-1 home draw against Lillestrom, before losing 1-0 away to Olympiacos. They have therefore collected four points from their opening three matches.
 One concern for Priske is his team’s lack of goals: Sparta have failed to score in four of their last five matches in all competitions. However, their home record in Europe offers encouragement, with just one defeat in their last nine UEFA home fixtures.
 Sparta will have to cope with several absences. Matej Rynes, Adam Karabec, Magnus Kofod Andersen and Emmanuel Uchenna are sidelined through injury. John Mercado, who has scored seven goals this season, is also a doubt after missing the last two matches with a calf problem.

 AFC Bournemouth - Riding a winning streak
 Let’s turn our attention to AFC Bournemouth. We will analyse the team’s momentum, recent results, and standout players for their upcoming trip to Prague.
 Recent form
 Bournemouth travel to Prague in exceptional form. Marco Rose’s side have won their last six matches in all competitions , scoring 16 goals without conceding.
 Their recent run includes three consecutive 3-0 victories over AC Milan, Manchester United and Aston Villa, followed by a 2-0 home win against Leeds United. The Cherries have also won three Premier League matches in a row without conceding for the first time in their history.
 Their European campaign has been equally impressive. Bournemouth began with a 2-1 away victory over Real Sociedad, followed by a 3-0 home win against Sturm Graz and another 3-0 success against AC Milan. They are among the five teams with a perfect record after the opening three rounds of the league phase.
 Bournemouth will not, however, have their full squad available. Alex Scott is nearing a return from a hamstring injury but is not expected to feature, while Alex Toth and Julián Araujo remain sidelined with thigh problems. Bafodé Diakité could replace James Hill in central defence.

 Predictions for Sparta Praha vs. AFC Bournemouth - Cherries' European dominance
 AFC Bournemouth arrives in Prague with impressive momentum, winning their last five matches across all competitions. Their attack has been clinical in Europe, making it very likely there will be over 0.5 goals in the first half.
 In contrast, Sparta Praha has struggled for consistency, with mixed results in their recent fixtures. Considering the visitors’ solid defence, which has conceded only once in Europe, there is a strong chance both teams will not score before half-time.
 Given the Cherries’ dominant form and the hosts’ inconsistent performances, our main prediction is an away victory. Therefore, we are backing AFC Bournemouth to win the match with a “-0.5” Asian Handicap .
